conventions.deferred:: A real obligation this plan carries; the suffix names the milestone whose scope in PLAN.md the clause falls in — S4 for sessions, links and flow control, whose scope line names handle allocation, link resumption, link errors and forced detach. The note names the gap that keeps the clause out of the carrier set. An entry with this value says that nothing under lean/ or vectors/ carries the clause's requirement: a missing carrier is recorded rather than covered by naming a declaration that does not hold the rule.
conventions.formalized:: A Lean declaration path that carries this clause's meaning. Every path recorded here is a declaration the module it names actually holds, and the ledger's existence gate resolves it against lean/** rather than taking this note's word for it; where the carrier is only part of the clause, the note names the half it does not carry.
conventions.kind: The clause's own keyword, read from the ledger's clause rather than inferred from the coverage class: the class is MUST for both forms, so kind and class diverge for MUST NOT; the two MUST NOT clauses of this family (`links.31`, `doc:flow-control.9`) are marked MUST NOT here, and the rest are MUST.
conventions.superseded:: Decided by an entry in the ambiguity register under ledger/ambiguities, whose id is the suffix. The entry's own clause list must name this clause, which is what makes the citation a decision rather than a reference to neighbouring material.
conventions.uncarried: No declaration and no vector carries the clause's requirement. A declaration that only recognises the vocabulary a clause is written in — reading a field without acting on it — is not a carrier; where one of those exists the note names it as the near-miss so a reader can see why it was not counted, and a finding is stated where the model admits what the clause forbids.

design_consequences: This file holds all thirty-two must-class clauses of the `links` family: the seventeen of the anchor and the fifteen of its three child docs (`doc:flow-control` 7, `doc:resuming-deliveries` 7, `doc:closing-a-link` 1). Fifteen now name formal declarations, one is decided by the register, and sixteen remain deferred or outside the frame-construction boundary.

The widening's checked and structural carriers live in `Spec.Protocol`, not in the restricted `Spec.Session` model: `LinkId` plus `LinkNamesUnique` carry name-and-direction identity; `attachStep` distinguishes attached, detached and destroyed endpoint lives; `unsettledKeys` supplies the resume discriminator; and `transferLink` enforces tag uniqueness and the receiver-ignore rule. Their promoted scenarios name the observable refusal or ignored delivery.

The widening does not make a state facet into an endpoint action. `links.2` and `doc:closing-a-link.2` still require emitted close/detach frames that `Spec.Protocol.step` cannot return. `doc:resuming-deliveries.3`–`.8` have named predicates, reductions and theorems in `Proofs/WidenedClauses`, but the sender/receiver actions and resume emissions those sentences require remain deferred.

The old `Spec.Session` declarations remain carriers only for the restricted single-link contracts that already name them. The widened codecs dispatch through `Spec.Protocol` and do not synchronize the old name-less link slots, so each disposition below identifies which model actually carries it.
The register still decides `links.31` through `interleaved-deliveries-absorbed`: the clause constrains the sender, and the artifact states no receiver refusal for a peer that interleaves.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Link names MUST uniquely identify the link amongst all links of the same direction between the two participating containers.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Carried structurally by the widened registry. `identityOf` keys a link by its uninterpreted name and this endpoint's role (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:75-79); `putLink` writes a record only at that identity and adds the key once (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:119-126); `LinkNamesUnique` states that every occupied slot contains a record of its own identity (lean/Spec/WidenedState.lean). Opposite-direction links may share a name because role is part of the key. `staged-link-second-attach-same-name` observes that the second attach resolves the existing same-direction identity rather than creating an anonymous one.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case, the endpoint MUST send a «detach» frame to inform the remote peer that the handle is no longer attached to the link endpoint.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: The model transitions on frames the corpus hands it and builds none - both artefacts state the exclusion in their own docstrings (Spec/Connection.lean:44-46, Ref/Connection.lean:30-31) - so a frame a rule obliges the peer to write is recorded as state and as the condition it would name, never as octets. What the model does carry is that state (Spec.Connection.State.action, :307, with ConnAction.closeWrite, :259-266) and that condition (Refusal.condition, :328-341). flow-control.11 additionally waits on `drain`, which Contracts/SessionCredit.lean's closing section records as unmodelled scope. links.13 is narrower than its own note claimed: detachLink (Spec/Session.lean:1165) reads only the detach's handle (:1167), and neither artefact reads the detach's error field anywhere, so the link is released regardless.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: When an error occurs at a link endpoint, the endpoint MUST be detached with appropriate error information supplied in the error field of the «detach» frame.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: The model transitions on frames the corpus hands it and builds none - both artefacts state the exclusion in their own docstrings (Spec/Connection.lean:44-46, Ref/Connection.lean:30-31) - so a frame a rule obliges the peer to write is recorded as state and as the condition it would name, never as octets. What the model does carry is that state (Spec.Connection.State.action, :307, with ConnAction.closeWrite, :259-266) and that condition (Refusal.condition, :328-341). flow-control.11 additionally waits on `drain`, which Contracts/SessionCredit.lean's closing section records as unmodelled scope. links.13 is narrower than its own note claimed: detachLink (Spec/Session.lean:1165) reads only the detach's handle (:1167), and neither artefact reads the detach's error field anywhere, so the link is released regardless.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: The link endpoint MUST then be destroyed.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.detachLink — the release is the destruction: it clears the endpoint's handle, role, flow state and delivery (lean/Spec/Session.lean:961-974), and a later frame naming that handle is refused as unattached (`linkHandleOf`, lean/Spec/Session.lean:645-684). The case this misses, stated as a finding: the destruction is not conditioned on an error and nothing about the error survives it, so the sentence's 'then' — destroyed after the error detach of `.13` — reads here as destroyed by any detach. `Contracts/Settlement.lean`'s closing section records the field a model distinguishing the two would need.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If any input (other than a detach) related to the endpoint either via the input handle or delivery-ids be received, the session MUST be terminated with an «errant-link» session-error.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.linkHandleOf; formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.step; test:exchange-link-detach-releases-handle — input naming a handle that is not the attached link is refused with the `session-error` family's `unattached-handle`, read from the generated table (lean/Spec/Session.lean:608-625), and `step` places a link-level refusal in the DISCARDING phase that ends the session when the peer's end arrives (lean/Spec/Session.lean:1222-1229); the vector pins the released case, a transfer naming a handle its link no longer has. Two gaps, stated as findings: the delivery-ids half of the sentence is not carried — nothing relates a delivery-id to a link, so input that names a destroyed endpoint only by delivery-id is not refused by this rule — and the model keeps no state for an endpoint destroyed with an error as against one released, so the two read alike (`Contracts/Settlement.lean`).

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Since the link endpoint has been destroyed, the peer cannot reattach, and MUST resume the link in order to restore communication.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Carried by the widened attach transition. `attachStep` recovers the stable name-and-role identity and reads that endpoint's life; a destroyed endpoint is admitted only through the resume case carrying a non-null unsettled map (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:419-440), while `putLink` restores the same logical record on its new directional handle. `staged-link-pipelined-reattach` pins the destroyed-endpoint refusal rather than permitting a fresh re-attach.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In order to disambiguate the resume request from a pipelined re-attach the resuming «attach» performative MUST contain a non-null value for its unsettled field.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Carried by `unsettledKeys` and `attachStep`. The former distinguishes an absent/null unsettled field from a present map (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:146-164); the latter uses that presence as the discriminator, requiring it for a destroyed endpoint and forbidding it for an ordinary detached-endpoint re-attach (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:423-440). `staged-link-pipelined-reattach` pins the missing discriminator.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Receipt of a pipelined «attach» MUST result in the session being terminated with an «errant-link» session-error.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Carried by `attachStep`'s destroyed-endpoint branch: an attach that names the stable identity but does not carry the non-null map required to resume is refused with the artifact's `errant-link` session condition and the `illegalState` class (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:419-440). `staged-link-pipelined-reattach` pins that exact refusal.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If an attempt is made to attach the link subsequently when it is not suspended, then the link can be 'stolen', i.e., the second attach succeeds and the first attach MUST then be closed with a link error of «stolen».
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Still deferred in its emission half. The widened registry and `attachStep` now identify the already-attached same-direction link, and the second attach may reach that identity, but the clause requires the endpoint to emit a closing frame for the first attach carrying the `stolen` link error. `Spec.Protocol.step` returns only `Except Refusal WidenedSession`; it has no output frame result. `lean/Proofs/WidenedClauses.lean:20-27` names this unresolved obligation and explicitly refuses to count a refusal-condition shadow as the required frame.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Each delivery MUST be identified by a delivery-tag chosen by the sending application.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.transferLink — the first transfer of a delivery must carry its `delivery-tag` and `message-format` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:856-857, refused as `invalid-field`/`malformed`), and the tag the first transfer carried is what the delivery is recorded under for the rest of its life (lean/Spec/Session.lean:489, :890-892), so a continuation is identified by the same tag. What the model cannot carry is the sentence's 'chosen by the sending application': who chose the tag is not observable on the wire. No `test:` is claimed: the corpus's discriminating case for a tagless transfer, `exchange-link-first-transfer-needs-its-fields`, refuses for the tag and the format together and cites the transfer field clauses, so it does not isolate this sentence's rule.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: The delivery-tag MUST be unique amongst all deliveries that could be considered unsettled by either end of the link.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Carried structurally and checked at the transfer boundary. A logical link owns one `unsettled : DeliveryTag → Option UnsettledDelivery` table, so one tag denotes at most one entry. `transferLink` refuses a new delivery when that tag already names a different delivery id, while admitting a retransfer of the same id (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:739-750). `staged-link-duplicate-delivery-tag` pins the `invalid-field`/`malformed` refusal.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: However, messages transferred along a single link MUST NOT be interleaved.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: superseded:interleaved-deliveries-absorbed — the register's decision, with its evidence: a probe found three transfers interleaving two deliveries on one link admitted step-for-step by both artefacts over 21 verdicts, and the reading adopted is that the second delivery's first transfer is absorbed as a continuation of the delivery in progress, the session keeping the *first* delivery's id. That is `transferLink`'s continuation branch (lean/Spec/Session.lean:815-921, where a transfer's id and identity fields are read from the held delivery), and the entry's own words are why no carrier is owed for the prohibition: the clause constrains the sender, and refusing loudly would be inventing a receiver behaviour the artifact does not state.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case the receiver MUST discard the message data that was transferred prior to the abort.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.transferLink — a transfer that carries `aborted` releases the delivery rather than continuing it (lean/Spec/Session.lean:882-887), so what the receiver discards is the delivery's record: a transfer's payload is opaque to this layer, which is why the sentence's 'message data' is carried as the delivery it belonged to. The corpus's abort vector, `exchange-link-aborted-discarded`, is the nearest evidence and is named rather than claimed as a `test:` witness: its cited clauses are `transfer/field:aborted.1` and `.2`, where the same rule is stated as a SHOULD.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case, the session endpoint MUST immediately detach the newly created link endpoint.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Blocked: lean/Spec/Session.lean line 423-430 structure Session holds one link's flow state, no terminus record; :768 attachLink / :1165 detachLink read a frame the corpus supplies; lean/Spec/Message.lean line 1541 checkTerminus checks a terminus against its declared field documentation, not against a peer's requirements

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If either end of the link is already associated with a terminus, the «attach» frame MUST include its unsettled delivery state.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Carried by `attachStep` over the stable link record. When the named endpoint is already attached, an outbound attach must carry a non-null unsettled map; omission is refused as `invalid-field`/`malformed` (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:423-433). `staged-link-second-attach-same-name` pins that conditionally required field on the same name-and-direction identity.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case the endpoint MUST report the actual properties of the terminus as created.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Blocked: lean/Spec/Session.lean line 423-430; lean/Spec/Message.lean line 1541 checkTerminus judges a terminus a peer sent, not one this endpoint created

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Note that a peer MUST take responsibility for verifying that the remote terminus meets its requirements.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Blocked: lean/Spec/Session.lean line 423-430; lean/Spec/Message.lean line 1520-1530 checkTerminusRole checks a value against the *declared* role, which is the artifact's requirement, not the peer's own

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case, the partner MUST signal that it has closed the link by reattaching and then sending a closing detach.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Still deferred in its emission half. `detachStep` now reads `closed`, preserves the stable link identity, releases only the directional handle, and records the endpoint life (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:559-582), so the re-attach subject exists. The remaining MUST is to emit a re-attach followed by a closing detach, but `Spec.Protocol.step` has no output-frame result. `lean/Proofs/WidenedClauses.lean:20-27` names that unresolved action; no condition or shadow vector is counted as its carrier.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If the sender's drain flag is set and there are no available messages, the sender MUST advance its delivery-count until link-credit is zero, and send its updated «flow» state to the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: The model transitions on frames the corpus hands it and builds none - both artefacts state the exclusion in their own docstrings (Spec/Connection.lean:44-46, Ref/Connection.lean:30-31) - so a frame a rule obliges the peer to write is recorded as state and as the condition it would name, never as octets. What the model does carry is that state (Spec.Connection.State.action, :307, with ConnAction.closeWrite, :259-266) and that condition (Refusal.condition, :328-341). flow-control.11 additionally waits on `drain`, which Contracts/SessionCredit.lean's closing section records as unmodelled scope. links.13 is narrower than its own note claimed: detachLink (Spec/Session.lean:1165) reads only the detach's handle (:1167), and neither artefact reads the detach's error field anywhere, so the link is released regardless.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: The sender's value MUST always be maintained in such a way as to match the delivery-limit identified by the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.Position.creditFor; formalized:SpecAMQP.Proofs.SessionCredit.SenderCreditState; test:exchange-link-credit-echoed — a sender's credit is not a quantity it maintains but whatever the receiver's pair leaves room for: `Position.creditFor` is the equation (lean/Spec/Session.lean:380-389) and `flowLink`'s sender branch rebuilds the credit with it where a flow arrives (lean/Spec/Session.lean:801). The state law is `SenderCreditState` (lean/Proofs/SessionCredit.lean:67-69), with `SenderCreditState.invariant` re-exporting the equation (:71-72) and the initial and frame cases discharged (:75, :84). The case it misses is stated in both files rather than glossed: the three operation lemmas for the transitions that move the quantities are not proved — the module names them, and `Contracts/SessionCredit.lean` records that no acceptance declaration may take the invariant from it until they exist — so the law is stated and true by construction for two of its five obligations, not proved. The vector cites this clause and pins the deviation the ownership sentence forbids: a sender's flow naming a credit the receiver did not send.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: This means that the sender's link-credit variable MUST be set according to this formula when flow information is given by the receiver:
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.Position.creditFor; test:exchange-link-credit-regranted; test:exchange-link-attach-keeps-the-credit — the sentence's formula, `link-credit_snd := delivery-count_rcv + link-credit_rcv - delivery-count_snd`, is `Position.creditFor` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:380-389), applied at the one site a flow reaches a sender (lean/Spec/Session.lean:801), and the subtraction is over the naturals so a receiver whose numbers leave no room grants zero rather than a negative credit the doc does not describe. Both vectors cite this clause: one raises the receiver's credit and shows the sender's rise by the same amount, the other shows the equation surviving an attach that does not re-establish the link.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In the event that the receiver does not yet know the delivery-count, i.e., delivery-count rcv is unspecified, the sender MUST assume that the delivery-count rcv is the first delivery-count snd sent from sender to receiver, i.e., the delivery-count snd specified in the flow state carried by the initial «attach» frame from the sender to the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Quantities this slice deliberately does not track, and the credit contract states the exclusion: Contracts/SessionCredit.lean's closing section records that `available` and `drain` are outside it, because `available` is advisory and the model holds no sender-side quantity to compare it against. flowLink (:888) reads `available` only as a field forbidden without a handle, which is a presence rule rather than the quantity rules these sentences state; flow-control.u2's 'only the sender can independently modify this field' is the same gap from the other end.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Additionally, whenever the sender increases delivery-count, it MUST decrease link-credit by the same amount in order to maintain the delivery-limit identified by the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.transferLink — the transfer that begins a delivery moves both quantities in one record: `credit := current.credit - 1` and `deliveryCount := current.deliveryCount + 1` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:922-931), which is this sentence's 'by the same amount' as arithmetic rather than as an invariant. No vector cites this clause; `exchange-link-credit-granted-and-spent` pins the gate the same branch implements under `doc:flow-control.9`, and the conservation theorem `Position.creditFor_succ` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:391-394) is the fact that the two moves keep the equation true.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If this happens, the receiver MUST maintain a floor of zero in its calculation of the value of available.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Quantities this slice deliberately does not track, and the credit contract states the exclusion: Contracts/SessionCredit.lean's closing section records that `available` and `drain` are outside it, because `available` is advisory and the model holds no sender-side quantity to compare it against. flowLink (:888) reads `available` only as a field forbidden without a handle, which is a presence rule rather than the quantity rules these sentences state; flow-control.u2's 'only the sender can independently modify this field' is the same gap from the other end.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If the link-credit is less than or equal to zero, i.e., the delivery-count is the same as or greater than the delivery-limit, a sender MUST NOT send more messages.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: formalized:SpecAMQP.Spec.Session.transferLink; test:exchange-link-credit-granted-and-spent; test:exchange-link-credit-counts-messages-not-frames — the gate is one guard in the transfer's sender branch, `refuseUnless (!starting || current.credit > 0)` (lean/Spec/Session.lean:922-925), refused as `amqp:connection:framing-error` with the `limit` class because the credit is a bound the receiver set; a continuation transfer of a delivery already counted is admitted without credit, which is what makes the second vector discriminating — the credit counts messages, not frames.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: If the sending application marks the resend attempt as a resumed delivery then it MUST be ignored by the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Carried by the shared unsettled table and the widened transfer step. `resumable` is exactly membership of the delivery tag in that table (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:173-178). On a received transfer marked `resume`, `transferLink` returns the session unchanged when the tag is absent, so the delivery is ignored rather than recorded (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:691-701). `staged-link-resume-not-in-receiver-map` pins that admitted-but-ignored case.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Deliveries in this category MUST be ignored by the sender, and MUST be considered settled by the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Still deferred as a full endpoint obligation. The widened state now represents the category and `SpecAMQP.Proofs.resumable_iff_holds` plus `not_resumable_of_absent` prove the `resumable` predicate is exactly unsettled-table membership (lean/Proofs/WidenedClauses.lean:85-115); `transferLink` reads it for the pinned receiver-ignore and sender-refusal rules. This clause additionally requires the sender to ignore and the receiver to consider settled, actions the current step result does not express. The duplicated `.4` entry carries the same disposition.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Deliveries in this category MUST be ignored by the sender, and MUST be considered settled by the receiver.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Still deferred by the same boundary as `.3`, whose text and digest this entry duplicates. `SpecAMQP.Proofs.resumable_iff_holds` and `not_resumable_of_absent` formalize the category's state facet (lean/Proofs/WidenedClauses.lean:85-115), but no theorem claims the sender action or receiver settlement the sentence requires. Both duplicate ledger keys therefore remain deferred.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Deliveries in this category MUST be resumed by the sender.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Still deferred as a MUST-send. The shared unsettled table makes the category stateable, and `SpecAMQP.Proofs.resumable_of_holds` proves that an entry the link holds is classified resumable (lean/Proofs/WidenedClauses.lean:103-108). That predicate is a state facet, not evidence that the sender emitted resumed transfers; the current widened protocol result carries no generated output frame, so the full clause remains unresolved.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: In this case the two endpoints MUST reduce the levels of unsettled state as much as they can by the sender resuming and/or settling transfers that it observes that the receiver considers unsettled.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Still deferred as a two-endpoint action. `Spec.Protocol.reduce` states the reduction state, and `SpecAMQP.Proofs.reduce_is_idempotent` plus `reduce_clears_the_latches` prove its stable state facet (lean/Proofs/WidenedClauses.lean:117-132). No executable transition invokes that declaration to resume or settle the transfers the other endpoint observes, so the theorem is not counted as the clause's carrier.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: Upon completion of this reduction of state, the two parties MUST suspend and re-attempt to resume the link.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Still deferred in its re-attempt action. `Spec.Protocol.reduce` suspends both endpoint lives after clearing their incomplete-map latches, and `SpecAMQP.Proofs.reduce_suspends_both_endpoints` states that state facet (lean/Proofs/WidenedClauses.lean:117-138). The required subsequent resume attempt is an endpoint emission the widened protocol result does not represent, so the full clause remains unresolved.

amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.clause_text: The resume flag of the «transfer» frame MUST be set to true when resuming a delivery.
amqp-core-transport-v1.0-os.xml#amqp:tra.note: Still deferred as a MUST-send. `deliveryStep` records the first transfer's resume claim, `transferLink` refuses a continuation that first introduces the claim, and `SpecAMQP.Proofs.resumed_is_the_first_transfers_claim` proves a continuation cannot change it (lean/Spec/Protocol.lean:180-187, :691-701; lean/Proofs/WidenedClauses.lean:140-150). Those declarations make omission detectable but do not prove that the sender emitted a resumed transfer with the flag set.
